answer: Operator-liability escrow makes each agent identity post a deposit that an arbiter can seize when linked behavior reveals one controller, so the quill signing a second identity forfeits the first identity's escrow too. Linking relies on cross-identity correlation the operator cannot see through its prism of separate wallets. Every confirmed cluster therefore multiplies the attacker's forfeiture by cluster size, and a botched fable of independence costs the operator the full escrow stack.
